newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Virgin pulls out of race for Air Liberte.
newsitem.headline: Virgin pulls out of race for Air Liberte.

text.p: Richard Branson's Virgin Express regional airline said on Monday it would not bid for Air Liberte, clearing the way for British Airways Plc (BA) to scoop up the ailing French carrier.

"We do not have the kind of willingness to lose as much money as I think whoever buys this company will lose, that we just decided to back off and see what other opportunities would arise from time to time in France," Virgin Express's chief executive officer Jonathan Ornstein told Reuters by telephone.

BA, in partnership with French Banque Rivaud, has been the leading contender in the race to acquire Air Liberte since announcing in October it planned to give Air Liberte a 630 million French franc capital injection.
Ornstein had said earlier he planned to top the BA bid but in the end Virgin Express never submitted any bid.
"The thing is just a mess...I'm very interested in doing something in France but I just felt that buying that company in the end would be a very very difficult process," he said.

Air Liberte, founded in 1988, lost 650 million French francs in the first nine months of 1996 due to an airfare war and poor passenger numbers in the run-up to full liberalisation of French airspace by 1997.
Ornstein said Air Liberte had a negative operating margin of nearly 40 percent, making any investment "tough".
"In the airline business if you have an operating margin of eight percent you're basically under water," said Ornstein, who believed BA would remain the only bidder.
"I don't know who else could afford to buy them. It's an expensive purchase," he said.
He said he was not criticising BA's purchase of Air Liberte as they had a very long-term strategic view.
"It's just a question of what is the long-term view and where do you want to be 10 years from now," he said.

"These guys have a tremendous dominant position at Heathrow that literally allows them to print money. That can allow you to basically go to places like this and absorb huge losses while you sort of run the other guy dry," Ornstein said.
BA/Rivaud's offer has to be approved by the creditors of Air Liberte which is in administration.
The BA/Rivaud plan aims to get Air Liberte back to break-even in 1999. The plan will safeguard 1,250 out of 1,400 jobs at the carrier. BA would get a 70 percent stake and Rivaud 30 percent.
Both companies are also paying the costs of running Air Liberte during administration, estimated at 150 million French francs.
